Parse a year or year-quarter period column into a time Date column

Source: R/oecd_funs.R
parse_period_date.Rd

A small stand-in for pxwebtools::parse_dates(), covering only the two period formats this package's own code needs: "Y" (a 4-digit year, e.g. "2021") and "y-q" (year and quarter, e.g. "2021-Q1", as OECD's quarterly data uses), each mapped to the first day of that year or quarter. As with parse_dates(), the parsed column always ends up named time, replacing whatever column date_format's name pointed at.

Usage

parse_period_date(df, date_format)

Arguments

df

A data frame.

date_format

A single named character vector, c(<column> = "Y") or c(<column> = "y-q"): the column to parse and which format it is in.

Value

df, with date_format's column parsed into a Date and renamed to time.

Examples

parse_period_date(data.frame(year = c("2020", "2021")), c(year = "Y"))
#>         time
#> 1 2020-01-01
#> 2 2021-01-01
parse_period_date(data.frame(obsTime = c("2021-Q1", "2021-Q2")),
                  c(obsTime = "y-q"))
#>         time
#> 1 2021-01-01
#> 2 2021-04-01
